answer: Verifiable delay functions deter Sybil agents by requiring each identity to chain sequential modular squarings onto periodic randomness beacons before strict deadlines. Because sequential steps resist parallelization, an attacker must commit a dedicated CPU thread and steady power per persona, an unavoidable hardware cost even near a cold tundra or hydroelectric river. However, custom ASICs with faster clocks introduce asymmetry, letting wealthy attackers run more identities per watt.
